title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 60 (Publication of Authorised, Subscribed and Paid-Up Capital)

content.overview: Section 60 requires that where any notice, advertisement or other official publication, or any business letter, billhead or letter paper of a company contains a statement of the amount of the authorised capital of the company, such notice or document must also contain a statement, in an equally prominent position and in equally conspicuous characters, of the amount of the capital which has been subscribed and the amount paid-up.
content.glance: If authorised capital is stated in notices, ads or stationery, subscribed and paid-up capital must also be stated equally prominently.
content.study: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 60 (Publication of authorised, subscribed and paid-up capital). If a notice, advertisement or other official publication, or a business letter, billhead or letter paper of a company states the amount of authorised capital, it must also state the amount of subscribed capital and paid-up capital in an equally prominent position and equally conspicuous characters. The trigger is the statement of authorised capital in one of the specified communications; the duty is to disclose both subscribed and paid-up figures with equal prominence. Section 60 is a disclosure rule, not the procedure for altering share capital under section 61. Any separate penalty or compliance consequence should be identified only after checking the applicable current provision.

sections.heading: Trigger
sections.body: A notice, advertisement, other official publication, business letter, billhead or letter paper of the company states its authorised capital.

sections.heading: Required additional figures
sections.body: The same communication must state both subscribed capital and paid-up capital.

sections.heading: Equal prominence
sections.body: The subscribed and paid-up figures must appear in an equally prominent position and in equally conspicuous characters as the authorised-capital statement.

sections.heading: Distinction from capital alteration
sections.body: Section 60 governs disclosure of capital figures. Section 61 governs specified alterations to share capital; section 60 does not itself authorise an alteration.

provisions.title: Publication of authorised, subscribed and paid-up capital

examples.title: Compliant stationery
examples.body: Letter paper states authorised ₹10 crore, subscribed ₹6 crore and paid-up ₹5 crore in equally prominent characters. Section 60 is complied with.

examples.title: Misleading advertisement
examples.body: An advertisement states only ‘Authorised capital ₹100 crore’ without subscribed or paid-up figures. Section 60 is breached.

hypotheticals.question: Can a company advertise only its authorised capital?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. If authorised capital is stated, subscribed and paid-up must also be stated equally prominently under s. 60.

distinctions.title: Capital disclosure and capital alteration
distinctions.left: Section 60 governs how authorised, subscribed and paid-up capital are disclosed.
distinctions.right: Section 61 governs how a limited company may alter share capital.

rows.left: Prominence of capital figures in communications

rows.right: Capital alteration power subject to statutory conditions

misconceptions.trap: Stating authorised capital alone is always fine.
misconceptions.correction: Section 60 requires subscribed and paid-up to be stated equally prominently whenever authorised capital is stated.

questionsAndAnswers.question: When does section 60 require subscribed and paid-up capital to be disclosed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Whenever authorised capital is stated in one of the specified company publications or stationery.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How must the figures appear?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Subscribed and paid-up capital must be stated in an equally prominent position and equally conspicuous characters.
